name: BASS
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) + SPICE fan-driven flow duct
fuels: Flat samples, PMMA (acrylic) spheres, porous wax slabs, wax candles, cotton-fiberglass fabric
fuel_geometry: 2-cm acrylic spheres and 2-cm wide fabric strips in opposed flow; flat samples; wax slabs and candles
objective: Burns a wide variety of solid samples in the Microgravity Science Glovebox with airflow speed as the main variable, then applies nitrogen suppressant. Early results: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative (materials can burn at lower oxygen in microgravity), and local suppressant can fail or even strengthen a flame by entraining air.
o2_note: 21% O2 (ISS air) down to 17% using nitrogen, at 1 atm (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)
airflow: 0-30 cm/s (spacecraft ventilation range); example tests from 12 cm/s down to below 1 cm/s (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)

name: BASS-II
full_name: Burning and Suppression of Solids II
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) + SPICE fan-driven flow duct
fuels: Solid samples including fabric (sizes and oxygen range to verify in PSI)
fuel_geometry: Solid samples (sizes to verify in PSI)
objective: Follow-on to BASS extending solid-material flammability and suppression tests in the same flow duct.
o2_note: Oxygen varied; exact range to be verified in PSI

name: Saffire-I
hardware: Saffire large-scale flow-duct experiment module
fuel_geometry: Large sample in a flow duct (size to verify in PSI)
objective: First large-scale, spacecraft-relevant fire test, beyond the sample sizes possible inside ISS facilities, to validate small-scale flammability data.

name: Saffire-II
hardware: Saffire large-scale flow-duct experiment module
fuel_geometry: Large samples in a flow duct (sizes to verify in PSI)
objective: Follow-on large-scale fire test with additional materials and conditions.

name: Saffire-III
hardware: Saffire large-scale flow-duct experiment module
fuel_geometry: Large samples in a flow duct (sizes to verify in PSI)
objective: Further large-scale fire test extending material and condition coverage.

name: SAME
hardware: Smoke and aerosol measurement instrument
fuels: Smoke particles from heated spacecraft-like materials
objective: Measured the particle-size distribution of smoke from spacecraft materials, giving guidance for the design of future spacecraft smoke detectors.
earth_application: NASA smoke detector work discriminating smoke from dust reduced nuisance alarms on Earth.

name: SAME-R
full_name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight
hardware: Smoke and aerosol measurement instrument
fuels: Smoke from heated spacecraft-like materials, including Pyrell (intumescent fire-retardant)
objective: Reflight of SAME extending smoke measurements in microgravity for detector design.
earth_application: NASA smoke detector work discriminating smoke from dust reduced nuisance alarms on Earth.

name: DAFT
full_name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
hardware: Smoke and aerosol measurement instrument (same instrument as SAME)
objective: Measured background aerosol particulate levels on the ISS with the SAME instrument, informing how detectors can tell dust from smoke and avoid nuisance alarms.
earth_application: Dust-versus-smoke discrimination applies to terrestrial settings such as mining.

name: DAFT-2
full_name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test 2
hardware: Smoke and aerosol measurement instrument (same instrument as SAME)
objective: Measured background aerosol particulate levels on the ISS with the SAME instrument, informing how detectors can tell dust from smoke and avoid nuisance alarms.

name: FLEX
hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
fuel_geometry: Droplet 1-5 mm (MDCA range), fiber-supported or free floating
objective: Studies heptane and methanol droplets in O2/N2 mixtures with a second inert gas (N2, CO2, He, Xe) to see how suppressants shift the flammability limit. Key result: the limit is lower in reduced gravity, so terrestrial inert-gas suppressant standards give less margin of safety in space. Also uncovered stable cool flames that persist after the visible flame goes out.
o2_note: O2/N2 mixtures with an added inert diluent (N2, CO2, He or Xe). MDCA supports 0-3 atm and up to 40% O2. Example test: heptane in 21% O2, 70% CO2, balance N2 (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)
airflow: Droplet translated at 3 cm/s in the 70% CO2 example test
earth_application: Fine water-mist extinguishers developed for ISS have Earth applications.

name: FLEX-2
hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
fuels: Pure-fuel mixtures and real-fuel surrogates, e.g. ethanol and methyl butanoate droplets
fuel_geometry: Droplets, including droplet-droplet interaction and slow sub-buoyant flow studies
objective: Follow-on to FLEX: extends tests to fuels and conditions that mimic real combustors, including fuel mixtures, real-fuel surrogates, soot formation, slow sub-buoyant flow and droplet-droplet interactions.
o2_note: 10-40% O2 (0.1-0.4 mole fraction), 0.5-3.0 atm, diluent gas balance (PSI summary). Example: ethanol at 30% O2, 2.4 atm (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)

name: CFI
hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
fuel_geometry: Single suspended droplet (size to verify in PSI)
objective: Studies low-temperature cool flames of droplets. Relevant to fire safety but less directly than solid-material flammability.
o2_note: Oxygen not given in the PSI summary; pressure 0.25-5 atm (PSI summary)

name: CFI-G
hardware: ACME modular hardware in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
fuels: Propane, n-butane and n-pentane; normal and inverse flames
fuel_geometry: Spherical burner; oxidizer flows out of the burner into the fuel-filled chamber (inside-out flame)
objective: Highest-oxygen microgravity tests in PSI, with oxidizer up to 85% oxygen. Directly bounds the oxygen-enriched atmospheres expected in a Moon Base and pressurized rovers.

name: BRE
hardware: ACME modular hardware in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
fuels: A small number of gaseous fuels chosen to emulate paper, plastic and alcohol burning
fuel_geometry: Flat porous burner; fuel flow set from measured heat flux and surface temperature to mimic condensed-fuel vaporization (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)
objective: Fire prevention focus: improves understanding of materials flammability (ignition and extinction) and checks whether existing flammability test methods remain valid in low and partial gravity.

name: E-FIELD Flames
full_name: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (ACME)
hardware: ACME modular hardware in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
fuel_geometry: Coflow or simple gas-jet flame with a mesh electrode above the burner (up to 10 kV) (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)
objective: Uses electric fields on flame ions to mimic partial gravity. Closest analogue to Moon/Mars gravity in PSI; no true partial-gravity data exists yet.
sensors: Flame response time to electric forcing

name: CLD Flame
hardware: ACME modular hardware in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
fuels: Diluted methane and ethylene in an air coflow
fuel_geometry: Lifted coflow gas-jet flames (avoids heat loss to the burner) (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)
objective: Extends the flame conditions models can predict, at the extremes of fuel dilution: sooty pure-fuel flames and dilute flames near extinction. Builds on SLICE.

name: s-Flame
full_name: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (ACME)
hardware: ACME modular hardware in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
fuels: Hydrogen and methane (soot-free flames); ethylene (sooty flames); inert diluents in fuel and chamber
fuel_geometry: Spherical flame on a porous burner; fuel/inert mixture issues into the CIR chamber (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)
objective: Advances prediction of the structure, dynamics and extinction of soot-free and sooty flames: radiative and convective extinction limits, and pulsating instabilities.

name: Flame Design
hardware: ACME modular hardware in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
fuels: Ethylene or methane in an oxygen-enriched atmosphere
fuel_geometry: Spherical flame on a porous burner; inverse flame if approved, otherwise a coflow burner (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)
objective: Improves understanding of soot inception and control to enable oxygen-enriched combustion and burner designs that are robust and soot free. Tests soot-inception and extinction limits of spherical flames.
o2_note: Oxygen-enriched atmosphere; exact range not stated in the guide, verify in PSI

name: SPICE
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) + SPICE fan-driven flow duct
fuel_geometry: Laminar gas-jet diffusion flame in a fan-driven coflow duct
objective: Studies the transition from non-smoking to smoking flames (smoke point), an indicator of a fuel's tendency to produce soot, with the goal of simple predictions of soot emissions.
o2_note: Run in the Microgravity Science Glovebox, which is normally limited to ISS air (about 21% O2, 1 atm); verify in PSI (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)

name: SLICE
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) + SPICE fan-driven flow duct
objective: Studies the structure and stability of lifted and lifting flames, to advance combustion models that improve fuel efficiency and cut pollutants. Precursor to CLD Flame.
o2_note: Uses SPICE hardware in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (normally ISS air, about 21% O2, 1 atm); verify in PSI (ISS Combustion Science Researcher's Guide, 2015)

name: Cool Flame CFD
full_name: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: A Multidimensional Multi-Physics CFD Analysis
hardware: Computational modeling and analysis of PSI flight data
objective: Uses FLEX flight data from PSI to quantify how externally imposed thermal and convective perturbations affect cool flames, with a 3-D OpenFOAM model.

name: FGM Flame Spread
full_name: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling using Flamelet Generated Manifolds in Microgravity with Comparison to BASS Experiments using Two-Color Tomography
hardware: Computational modeling and analysis of PSI flight data
fuels: Solid fuel flame spread (modeled and compared with BASS)
objective: Develops and validates flamelet generated manifold (FGM) models of concurrent flame spread in microgravity, compared with BASS experiments.

name: SPICE Analysis
full_name: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets
hardware: Computational modeling and analysis of PSI flight data
objective: Combines image processing, diagnostics and soot modeling on SPICE images to explain the large soot difference between 1g and 0g flames. PSI notes results support safer fire detection and suppression.

name: Cool Flame Extinction
full_name: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation / Stretch Extinction Using Counterflow Flames
hardware: Computational modeling and analysis of PSI flight data
fuels: Cool flames under FLEX flight conditions (modeled)
objective: Uses FLEX conditions to compare oxygen concentration effects on cool flame extinction limits with three numerical models.

name: Smoke Growth Simulation
full_name: Utilization of the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Data for Advanced Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Micro-Gravity
hardware: Computational modeling and analysis of PSI flight data
objective: Uses numerical simulation, informed by SAME data, to explore how gravity changes pyrolysis smoke particle growth.
